description.value: The S.S. Moyie is the oldest known intact passenger-carrying sternwheel steamer in the world, built in 1898 for the Canadian Pacific Railway and now permanently ashore in Kaslo on Kootenay Lake. Designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1958, it offers tours of the original vessel—including the freight deck, saloon, pilot house, and paddlewheel—alongside a Visitor Centre, Gift Shop, Caboose, and the Kootenay Lake Archives. For a touring cyclist completing the Kootenay Lake loop, this waterfront site is a genuinely remarkable piece of BC and CPR history.

The OSM tags (tourism=museum, historic=heritage, phone, address) are consistent with the website content. Neither the website nor OSM tags mention bike-specific amenities, washrooms, water refill, food service, or any other cyclist-focused infrastructure, so those fields are null rather than false.
concerns: Website notes the Kootenay Lake Archives is temporarily closed due to renovation of the Kemball building, though the main ship and Visitor Centre remain open.
Phone number and physical address could not be independently confirmed from the website's scraped text; OSM values used as defaults.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A genuine, operating National Historic Site and world-class heritage attraction on a popular Kootenay Lake cycling route; a touring cyclist would clearly benefit from this listing as a destination stop.
enrichment_extras.notes: No cyclist-specific amenities (bike parking, washrooms, water) are mentioned anywhere on the website. An on-the-ground verification or direct inquiry could unlock several null fields.

wow_evidence: World's oldest intact passenger sternwheeler (1898), NHS since 1958 — world superlative with independent backing; touring the vessel is day-shaping, the story at dinner.
blurb: World's oldest intact passenger sternwheeler (1898), a National Historic Site on Kaslo's waterfront.
